question: According to the census of India 2011, which state among the following has the highest literacy rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, **Kerala** has the highest literacy rate among Indian states with a literacy rate of **94.00%**.
 
• Kerala's strong emphasis on education is attributed to the efforts of **missionary organizations** and early societal focus on literacy and schooling.
 
• The state has consistently maintained its leading position in literacy due to its **well-established education infrastructure** and policies.
 
• Kerala's female literacy rate is also the highest in India, reflecting **gender equality in educational access**.
 
• Other states with high literacy rates include Lakshadweep (91.85%) and Mizoram (91.33%), but Kerala remains at the top.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• Literacy rate refers to the percentage of people aged 7 and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.
 
 
 
• **Key Drivers of Kerala's Literacy:**
 
 
• Initiatives like the **Kerala State Literacy Mission** have played a pivotal role in achieving universal literacy.
 
• Strong policies promoting public education and **social reforms** by leaders like Sree Narayana Guru and Ayyankali have contributed significantly.
 
 
 
• **National Literacy Rate (2011):**
 
 
• The overall literacy rate of India, as per the 2011 Census, stands at **74.04%** with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Global Literacy:**
 
 
• India's literacy rate, though improving, still lags behind the global average of **86.3%** (as per UNESCO data).
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments:**
 
 
• The **New Education Policy 2020** emphasizes universal foundational literacy and numeracy to improve India's literacy landscape.
